questions.stem: A delta's requirement Outage cost has the text 'The planner charges each outage once a year.' and one scenario with a WHEN and a THEN step. What does strict validation report?

options.text: Nothing, since the requirement has a scenario with both steps
options.says: The page: text without SHALL or MUST is a warning, which strict mode fails on.

options.text: A warning for the missing SHALL or MUST, and the change fails
options.says: Right: a warning, and strict validation fails on warnings.

options.text: An error for the missing SHALL or MUST, so plain mode fails too
options.says: The page: it is a warning, and plain validation passes with two warnings.

options.text: A warning, and the change passes, since warnings never fail
options.says: The page: --strict fails on any warning.

origin.section: The Checker Applies the Format Rules That Strict Validation Applies

questions.stem: A planner proposes this requirement text for the cap: 'The planner SHALL add a row cap_y summing x over P_y, at most K.' Why does the page's approach reject it as spec text?

options.text: It lacks GIVEN and WHEN, which every requirement's text needs
options.says: The page: the text carries SHALL or MUST; steps belong in the scenarios under it.

options.text: It uses SHALL, which belongs only in a scenario's THEN step
options.says: The page: the requirement's text carries SHALL or MUST.

options.text: It states a cap, and caps are kept out of the living specs
options.says: The baseline spec has a Yearly start cap requirement.

options.text: It names a row and variables, which no planner can sign
options.says: Right: a spec names no variable, row or solver.

origin.section: A Requirement States One Behaviour With SHALL or MUST; a Scenario Says When and Then

questions.stem: You add a scenario and its test, and run the test on the code before the change. It passes. What does that passing run show about the test?

options.text: Nothing, since the test has never been seen to fail
options.says: Right: a test that has never failed has not shown that it tests anything.

options.text: That the old code keeps the rule, so the work is done
options.says: The page: a test that has never failed has shown nothing yet.

options.text: That the rule is checked, as the test is named after it
options.says: The page: a test that has never failed has not shown that it tests anything.

options.text: That the stub works, since a stub exists to pass tests
options.says: The page: the stub returns a wrong answer so each new test fails.

origin.section: Each Scenario Becomes a Test, and Each Test Fails Before the Code Exists
